containers.name: Policy Plus application
containers.tech: screens: TanStack Start, server rendered, with React 19, TanStack Router, Query and Form, Tailwind 4, shadcn on Base UI with Storybook for the components, lucide icons, Paraglide for the messages, Playwright for e2e tests

containers.name: Preference store
containers.tech: data: PostgreSQL through Drizzle on Effect SQL, with Drizzle Kit migrations

purpose: Policy Plus is a Windows desktop editor for Group Policy settings, used by administrators and power users. It reads Microsoft's policy definition files and edits policy files directly, so it works on any Windows edition, including Home, which lacks the built-in editor.

capabilities.name: Building and versioning Policy Plus
capabilities.purpose: Stamp the program with its current Git version when it is built.

capabilities.name: Getting Microsoft policy definitions
capabilities.purpose: Download Microsoft's current policy template package and unpack it into a folder the program can read.

capabilities.name: Using the product
capabilities.purpose: Product's own settings, such as the language of the policy text.

capabilities.name: Choosing and saving policy sources
capabilities.purpose: Pick where the user and computer policies are kept (POL file, registry, a user's registry hive, a user's Group Policy object, or the live system) and save changes back to them.

capabilities.name: Changing policy settings
capabilities.purpose: Set a policy to Enabled, Disabled or Not configured with its options and comment, and move settings in or out as SPOL text.

capabilities.name: Finding policies
capabilities.purpose: Narrow the policy list by filter and find policies by ID, text or registry key and value, then pick a result.

capabilities.name: Editing policy files directly
capabilities.purpose: Change the raw keys and values of a policy file, and bring registry files in or out of it.

capabilities.name: Browsing policy definitions
capabilities.purpose: Look through the loaded policy templates: categories, products, support rules, template files and policies, and open the details of each.

decisions.chose: Carried by apps/api: the Bun service runs on the person's own Windows machine and reads, writes and lists folders (POL files, template folders, export targets) directly with Bun and node:fs; the web app asks it through the HttpApi contract and never touches disk.
decisions.reason: Chose the local API over browser file pickers because the program must edit real policy files at fixed Windows paths and a browser sandbox cannot; assumes the service and the browser both run on the same machine as the files.

topic.system: Windows registry policy keys and loaded user hives

decisions.chose: Carried by apps/api: reads and writes policy keys, and loads and unloads user hives, by running reg.exe and PowerShell from Bun on the person's machine, behind one registry port that the domain layer sees only as plain data.
decisions.reason: Chose spawning the built-in Windows tools over a native Node addon because it needs no compiled dependency and works on Home editions; assumes the service runs elevated when writing machine policy and that the machine is Windows.

decisions.chose: Carried by apps/api: reads ADMX and ADML files from the chosen folders through the file system carrier and hands their text to the pure parsers in packages/domain; schemas for the parsed result live in packages/contracts.
decisions.reason: Chose parsing in the domain over parsing in the API handler so the rules stay pure and testable with fixture text; the API owns only reading bytes.

topic.system: Windows registry settings key of Policy Plus

decisions.chose: Replaced by the Preference store: remembered choices (language, definitions folder, offers considered) are rows in PostgreSQL through Drizzle in packages/database, reached by apps/api; the old registry key is not read or written.
decisions.reason: Chose the database that the confirmed architecture already includes over keeping a registry key because the Workspace domain is held by the Preference store container; the trade-off is that existing registry settings are not migrated, which is assumed acceptable (a one-time import can be a story if the owner wants it).

decisions.chose: Replaced: the Git version is stamped at build time by a script in packages/tooling that writes it into an environment value the API reports, instead of generating and compiling a version source file.
decisions.reason: Chose a build-time environment value over a generated source file because the TypeScript and Bun build has no compile step that needs one and a committed generated file goes stale.

decisions.chose: Carried by apps/api: reads and writes CMTX files beside the policy sources through the file system carrier, with the XML encoding and decoding in packages/domain.
decisions.reason: Chose keeping CMTX files on disk over storing comments in the database because Windows and other tools read these files in place; the API owns only the bytes.

decisions.chose: Carried by apps/api: resolves user and group accounts and their profile and policy-object locations by calling the machine's own Windows directory tools (PowerShell and ADSI) from Bun, on the person's machine, and returns a plain result or an unavailable status when no domain is reachable.
decisions.reason: Chose the local machine's directory access over a hosted lookup service because only the person's machine is joined to the domain with their credentials; assumes a domain may be absent, so the contract models unavailable as a normal outcome.

decisions.chose: Carried by apps/api: downloads the policy template package with Bun fetch from the Microsoft download site, extracts it into the chosen folder through the file system carrier, and reports progress and failure through the contract; the web app never calls the site itself.
decisions.reason: Chose server-side download over a browser download because the package must be unpacked into a Windows folder and the browser cannot write there; assumes internet access is optional and failure is a normal outcome.
